_doc: Water (story 16.8, AD-31, CAP-35). Lengths are base pixels (16 per tile). Every connected body of water tiles gets an organic shoreline: the tile edge is moved by seeded noise (`amp` px and `cell` px: small waves; `lobe`: wide bays and heads; `round`: blur radius that rounds the convex corners; `outward`: the share of a push past the tile edge that is kept, so the water pulls back far but only creeps over the land), so a pond or canal has no straight frame. The water itself is a mask image per body drawn by the water pipeline on Medium and High (render/pipelines/WaterFx.js) and, on Low and Canvas, as `fallback.frames` pre-drawn frames that loop at `fallback.fps` (render/waterMath.js draws both from the same formulas). Banks, stones, reeds and bridge piers are one static layer per body. `bands`: shore distances (px) where the depth colour steps from light to base to dark to deep. `foam`: the lapping foam band at the shore. `caustic`: shimmer in the shallows (distance in px). `swell`: wide slow bands (thresholds of a sine) one depth step lighter or darker, so open water is never one flat field. `ripple`: thin scrolling crests and troughs. `reflect`: lamps and lit windows in ctx.lights glint on the water within `reach` x their radius (at most `max` per body, nearest first). Banks are soft (sand and mud next to grass) or stone (next to paving).
